intro_en: "Oh, my Kinneret..." – the highlight of this segment of the Israel National Trail is the spectacular views of the Sea of Galilee (Kinneret) from different angles.
character_en: (For those walking from the north) Passage through agricultural land, planted forest and communities. Ascent of Mount Arbel, descent to the Kinneret moshava
pois_en: Arbel Fortress and the Mount Arbel cliff. Switzerland Forest. Ein Poriya. Hatzer Kinneret. Kinneret moshava
important_en: The ascent of Mount Arbel is long and steep, and the upper section is rocky; after rain it is slippery and dangerous for those descending it.
description_en:
We head south on a track running parallel to Road 90 and right beside it on the west. After a short walk the trail enters agricultural land, passing between mango, olive and citrus orchards.
We cross Road 807 at the junction of the entrance to the village of Hamam. The trail follows a compacted path (the entrance is to the right of the olive grove) bounded by two rows of stones; this section was prepared to serve those walking the "Gospel Trail".
The trail continues parallel to the channel of Nahal Arbel, passes near a cattle pen and climbs out of the channel onto a pavement at the edge of the village's entrance road.
The pavement leads us to a group of eucalyptus trees on the other side of the road. We enter between the trees through a gate, up the channel of Nahal Arbel. We pass between large jujube trees and reach a small spring, Ein Arbel.
Here the ascent of Mount Arbel begins. On the climbing trail, steps help hikers up the steep ascent. On the way up we see the Arbel Fortress, built in historical periods on the cliff of Mount Arbel (a visit to the fortress requires paying the national park entrance fee). The upper part of the ascent runs along the eastern side of the cliff.
Please note: the Israel National Trail does not pass through the more challenging section of the cliff, which has many metal rungs, but through the less steep eastern section. The route has rock steps and, in places, handholds to help. At the end of the climb, hikers receive a worthy reward: a beautiful view of the Kinneret, the Golan Heights and the Galilee.
Continuing south, the trail is gentle and easy.
We cross the Arbel Valley along its eastern edge on dirt tracks between cultivated fields and pastures. A beautiful view of the Kinneret accompanies us.
Near the community of Kfar Hittim the wide track becomes a path, leading along the edge of the community to the channel of Nahal Rakat. Up the channel we reach Road 7717, cross the road and continue to the community of Mitzpe. We cross the community and Road 77 on our way to the entrance to Upper Tiberias, Sapir Boulevard, the main street, along which we reach the edge of the neighbourhood and the entrance to the Switzerland Forest.
The route continues along tracks within the forest planted on the eastern slopes of the Poriya plateau towards the Kinneret. We pass several KKL-JNF picnic areas and lookout points over the Kinneret and the Golan. After crossing Road 7677, the trail passes into an agricultural area of orchards and citrus groves. Before the descent to the Kinneret moshava we pass Mitzpe Tamar and Ein Poriya. Beside the trail is a lovely picnic area in the shade of date palms, a recommended place to stop.
From here the trail descends to the Kinneret moshava. We pass through the moshava along HaMeyasdim Street to Hatzer Kinneret, the end point. Hatzer Kinneret is an organised site with an entrance fee; details on the website of the Council for Conservation of Heritage Sites in Israel.
nearby_en: Nabi Shu'ayb: the holiest site for the Druze.
The ancient synagogue near Moshav Arbel.
Tiberias: the lower city and its sites.
Kinneret Cemetery: burial place of the poet Rachel, Naomi Shemer, Berl Katznelson and other figures from the early days of settlement in the Jordan Valley.
Recommended lodging in the area: Alon Tavor Field School.
author_en: Itzik Ben Dov, trail marking coordinator at the Society for the Protection of Nature in Israel.
